title: Home at last
hook: airport goodbyes, a door closing, and the first word at the gate of the Garden
tomorrow: what if four little words were the whole map?

segments.voice: Yesterday: faces radiant, looking toward their Lord, like a clear moon nobody has to push to see. The journey home ends today, at a door.

Airport goodbyes have their own script. One more hug. Text me when you land. Did you pack your charger? Then a door closes behind you, and somewhere else, another door opens. The Qur'an describes the gates of the Garden, and the first word said there is one Muslims already say at every door: peace. The angels come in from every gate, it says, in Pickthall's words: "Peace be unto you because ye persevered."
screen: `TEXT ME WHEN YOU LAND.` → `A DOOR CLOSES, A DOOR OPENS.` → `PEACE, BECAUSE YE PERSEVERED.`

segments.voice: Peace runs all through the Qur'an's picture of the Garden. In one place, its people hear no idle talk there and no blame, only the saying: peace, and again peace. In another, their greeting there is: peace. Allah, the Qur'an says, calls to the abode of peace, dar al-salam. That's today's line: peace, peace. And notice that it's a homecoming word. A verse tells Muslims to greet one another when they enter houses, with a greeting from Allah, blessed and good, and so as-salamu alaykum is said walking through front doors every evening. Every one of those is a small rehearsal of the last door. The Qur'an doesn't picture the Garden as a hotel you check into alone. The same passage about the gates says the righteous of their parents, spouses and children enter with them. Family, gathered in, and a greeting at the gate. Look closely at the gate: the angels don't just say welcome. They say peace, because you kept going.
screen: `PEACE, AND AGAIN PEACE.` · `THE ABODE OF PEACE.` · `A GREETING AT EVERY DOOR.` · `FAMILY, GATHERED IN.` · then, large: `PEACE, PEACE.`

segments.voice: If you can, get up and walk slowly to the nearest door. Rest your hand on it for a breath, and as you step through, say salaam, or simply the word peace, to whoever is there, or to the empty room. Walk back the same slow way.
screen: `WALK TO THE NEAREST DOOR.` · `A HAND ON IT, ONE BREATH.` · `STEP THROUGH: PEACE.`

segments.voice: Home at last: the Garden as the Qur'an pictures it, a home with family gathered in, where the greeting at the gate is peace.
Two words for every doorway: peace, peace, said here and said at the last gate. The journey home is complete.

screen: `DAY 1776 COUNTS.` → `THE JOURNEY HOME · 11 OF 11.` → `TOMORROW: FOUR LITTLE WORDS, THE WHOLE MAP?`

chat.says: flying back to Chicago tonight. Dadi said 'go home safe.' but i AM home?? which one is home?
options: Both, for now. The Qur'an saves 'home at last' for the Garden, greeted with peace.
Here. Islam teaches your parents' house is the only place that counts as home.
Neither. Muslims are told not to call any place on earth their home at all.
chat.meaning: The Qur'an pictures the Garden as the last home: family gathered in, and the angels at every gate saying peace.
